heroText: Brussels is Belgium's multilingual capital, mixing guildhall grandeur, comic-strip walls, EU offices and serious food stops. Start at Grand Place, detour through the Galeries Royales Saint-Hubert, then visit the Atomium or Magritte Museum depending on your mood. Brussels Airport is the main gateway, with fast rail into the centre.

areas.name: Grand Place
areas.text: The Grand Place area is best for first-time sightseeing, restaurants and short walks to museums and covered galleries.

areas.name: Sablon
areas.text: Sablon is elegant and central, with antique shops, chocolate houses and easy access to museums and the palace area.

areas.name: Ixelles
areas.text: Ixelles has restaurants, bars and local neighbourhood energy, useful for longer stays beyond the tourist core.

areas.name: European Quarter
areas.text: The European Quarter is practical for EU institutions, business hotels and Parc du Cinquantenaire access.

airports.name: Brussels Airport (BRU)
airports.text: Brussels Airport is northeast of the city and has direct rail links to Brussels Central, Midi and North stations.

airports.name: Brussels South Charleroi Airport (CRL)
airports.search: Brussels South Charleroi Airport, Charleroi, Belgium
airports.text: Charleroi is used by low-cost airlines and sits much farther south, so allow longer coach or transfer time.

airportTransfer.value: 20 min by train from Brussels Airport to central stations
airportTransfer.note: Charleroi transfers take much longer by coach
airportTransfer.distance: about 12 km from BRU to central Brussels

stayOverview: Stay near Grand Place for a classic first visit, Sablon for museums and chocolate shops, Ixelles for food and nightlife, or the European Quarter for EU meetings and a quieter business-focused base.
hotelIntro: Brussels is easy by tram, metro and rail. The centre suits short sightseeing trips, Sablon feels polished, Ixelles is better for evenings, and the European Quarter is practical when meetings drive the schedule.
rentalCars: Do not rent for Brussels itself; trains are better for Bruges, Ghent, Antwerp and airport connections.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose Grand Place for a first short stay, or Sablon if museums, chocolate shops and quieter evenings matter.

travelTips.title: Airport choice
travelTips.text: Check the route from Brussels Airport (BRU) before choosing between a central hotel and an airport-area first night in Brussels.

travelTips.title: Transit
travelTips.text: Use contactless payment or transit passes on STIB-MIVB services rather than buying separate single tickets repeatedly.

travelTips.title: Day trips
travelTips.text: Bruges, Ghent and Antwerp are all easy rail day trips from Brussels Midi, Central or North.

history.text: According to local legend, the origin of the settlement that was to become Brussels lies in Saint Gaugericus' construction of a chapel on an island in the river Senne around 580.

When Otto II, Holy Roman Emperor, appointed the same Charles to become Duke of Lower Lotharingia in 977, Charles ordered the construction of the city's first permanent fortification, doing so on that same island.
In 1183, the Counts of Leuven became Dukes of Brabant.

history.label: 13th century
history.text: In the early 13th century, the first walls of Brussels were built and after this, the city grew significantly.
This palace, famous all over Europe, had greatly expanded since it had first become the seat of the Dukes of Brabant, but it was destroyed by fire in 1731.
It remained with Austria until 1795, when the Southern Netherlands were captured and annexed by France, and the city became the chef-lieu of the department of the Dyle.

The former Dyle department became the province of South Brabant, with Brussels as its capital. Late modern In 1830, the Belgian Revolution began in Brussels, after a performance of Auber's opera La Muette de.
The Free University of Brussels was established in 1834 and Saint-Louis University in 1858.
In 1835, the first passenger railway built outside England linked the municipality of Molenbeek-Saint-Jean with Mechelen.

The construction of the North–South connection, linking the main railway stations in the city, was completed in 1952, while the first premetro (underground tram) service was launched in 1969, and the first Metro line.

history.label: 1960s
history.text: Starting from the early 1960s, Brussels became the de facto capital of what would become the European Union (EU), and many modern offices were built.
